$comment: Places that mutate a runtime-identity variable process-wide. Entries are scoped to one function, never a whole file. Every entry needs a reason. A test that only needs its own home should state it through an explicit seam instead: PathResolver::new, TmuxRuntimeConfig.control_plane_args, or the child process's own env.

entries.reason: Production startup. It runs in main before Aimux creates worker threads, which is the one point where a process-wide export has no reader to race.
AimuxHomeEnvGuard, holding TEST_ENV_LOCK for the guard's lifetime. The loop self-report replay path resolves its home inside the call under test, so there is no seam to state it through yet.
The restore half of AimuxHomeEnvGuard, under the same held lock.
The isolated-runtime harness. It starts real daemon and project-service child processes that read their home from the environment, and holds ENV_LOCK from setup until drop.
The restore half of the isolated-runtime harness, under the same held lock.

log_lifecycle_always resolves its path from the environment inside the call under test, so there is no seam to state the home through. This binary holds a single test by design -- it fills the bounded failure ring, which would evict a sibling's record -- so the sibling reader this gate protects against does not exist. Adding a second test here must come with a lock or a different home.

Its own test binary holding a single test, matching async_runtime_failure_totals.rs. Asserting that a no-op scan writes NO log line needs process-wide logging pointed at a temp home, and there is no seam to pass a log sink through PeriodicTask::run.
